The ***Architecture Diagram*** given above explains the high-level design of the App.
The following provides a quick overview of the main components and their interactions.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F10-2/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F10-2/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.
* At app launch, it initializes the other components in the correct sequence, and connects them up with each other.
* At shut down, it shuts down the other components and invokes cleanup methods where necessary.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
* [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds the data of the App in memory.
* [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Reads data from, and writes data to, the hard disk.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) represents a collection of classes used by multiple other components.
**How the architecture components interact with each other**
The *Sequence Diagram* below illustrates the general interaction between the architecture components when a user
executes a command. Feature-specific interactions are documented in the [Implementation](#implementation) section.
Each of the four main components (also shown in the diagram above),
* defines its *API* in an `interface` with the same name as the Component.
* provides its functionality through a concrete `{Component Name}Manager` class that implements the corresponding API interface.

For example, the `Logic` component defines its API in `Logic.java` and implements it in `LogicManager.java`. Other components interact with a component through its interface rather than its concrete class, preventing them from coupling to that component's implementation, as illustrated in the following partial class diagram.
The sections below give more details of each component.
The **API** of this component is specified in [`Ui.java`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F10-2/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/Ui.java).
The UI consists of a `MainWindow` and its parts, such as `CommandBox`, `ResultDisplay`,
`CourseClassListPanel`, and `StatusBarFooter`. Course-class cards contain their enrolled students, homework status,
and notes. All of these, including `MainWindow`, inherit from the abstract `UiPart` class, which captures common
behavior among classes that represent visible GUI parts.
The `UI` component uses the JavaFX UI framework. The layouts of these UI parts are defined in matching `.fxml` files
* executes user commands using the `Logic` component.
* listens for changes to `Model` data so that the UI can be updated with the modified data.
* keeps a reference to the `Logic` component, because the `UI` relies on the `Logic` to execute commands.
* depends on classes in the `Model` component because it displays `CourseClass` and `Student` objects.
Here's a (partial) class diagram of the `Logic` component:
1. When `Logic` is called upon to execute a command, the command is passed to an `AddressBookParser` object, which
creates the matching feature parser where one is required.
1. This results in a `Command` object (for example, `AddCourseClassCommand`), which is executed by `LogicManager`.
1. The command can communicate with the `Model` when it is executed (for example, to add a course class).
Note that although this is shown as a single step in the diagram above for simplicity, the code can require several interactions between the command object and the `Model` to complete the operation.
1. The result of the command execution is encapsulated as a `CommandResult` object which is returned from `Logic`.
Here are the other classes in `Logic` (omitted from the class diagram above) that are used for parsing a user command:

* When called upon to parse a user command, the `AddressBookParser` class creates an `XYZCommandParser` (`XYZ` is a placeholder for the specific command name, e.g., `AddCommandParser`). The parser uses the other classes shown above to parse the user command and create an `XYZCommand` object (e.g., `AddCommand`). The `AddressBookParser` returns that object as a `Command` object.

* All `XYZCommandParser` classes, such as `AddCommandParser` and `DeleteCommandParser`, implement the `Parser` interface so they can be treated similarly where appropriate, for example during testing.
* stores the course-class book, including `CourseClass` objects, enrolled `Student` objects, notes, and homework status.
* exposes course classes selected by the current filter in an unmodifiable `ObservableList<CourseClass>` that the UI
can observe, so the displayed list updates when the model changes.
* stores snapshots of the course-class book for the persistent undo feature.
* stores a `UserPrefs` object that represents the user’s preferences (currently, just the GUI settings). This is exposed to the outside as a `ReadOnlyUserPrefs` object.
* does not depend on any of the other three components (as the `Model` represents data entities of the domain, they should make sense on their own without depending on other components)
* can save course-class data and user preference data in JSON format, and read them back into corresponding objects.
* is implemented by `StorageManager`, which delegates the actual file access to `JsonCourseClassBookStorage` and `JsonUserPrefsStorage`.
* uses `JsonSerializableCourseClassBook` to represent the current course-class book in JSON. Each item in `courseClasses` is represented by a `JsonAdaptedCourseClass`.

* stores the current course-class book and its `undoHistory` together in `data/courseclasses.json`. Each undo entry uses the same serializable structure and represents a complete previous `CourseClassBook` state.
* returns the current course-class book and its undo snapshots together through `CourseClassBookStorageData`, so the undo history is available after restarting the application.
* depends on some classes in the `Model` component because its job is to save and retrieve objects that belong to the `Model`.
Classes used by multiple components are in the `seedu.address.commons` package.

The `aclass` command creates a new `CourseClass` and adds it to the application's `CourseClassBook`. A course class
contains a class-group name, a course code, an optional set of tags, and an initially empty list of enrolled students.
`AddressBookParser` routes `aclass` to `AddCourseClassCommandParser`. The parser uses `ArgumentTokenizer` to read:
Both prefixes are required and may appear in either order. When `n/` appears first, the parser finds the following
`n/`, `t/`, `c/`, `m/`, `i/` and `o/` after a space when creating or renaming a class;
actual `t/` tags remain after `c/`. `t/` is optional and may be repeated; repeated identical tags are stored
once because tags are represented as a set. The parser rejects a non-empty preamble, missing required prefixes, and
duplicate `n/` or `c/` prefixes. `ParserUtil` validates the name, course code, and tags before the parser constructs

Only English letters, digits, spaces, `#`, `@` and `$` are allowed, and blank values are rejected.
`CourseCode` retains its previous validation so longer legacy codes remain loadable and usable in references.

`Model#addCourseClass` and returns a formatted success message containing the class name, course code, and tags.
`ModelManager#addCourseClass` delegates to `CourseClassBook`, then resets the filtered course-class list so the new
class is immediately visible in the UI. After a successful command, `LogicManager` records an undo snapshot and saves
the complete course-class book and undo history through `Storage#saveCourseClassBookData`, so the new class is

Compatibility: previously valid names such as `Group t/05` and course codes longer than 50 characters remain

The `hwork` command stores a class-wide `HomeworkStatus` on the selected `CourseClass`, together with optional
per-enrolment overrides keyed by telehandle. A student without an override inherits the class-wide status. The
override belongs to the class enrolment rather than the `Student` object because the same student may belong to
multiple classes with different homework states.
`AddressBookParser` routes `hwork` to `SetHomeworkStatusCommandParser`. The parser requires a positive displayed class
index and an `s/` status prefix, with an optional `t/` telehandle prefix. `ParserUtil` converts statuses to one of
`PENDING`, `COMPLETED`, or `NOT_SET`; the individual-only `inherit` value clears an override. During execution,
`SetHomeworkStatusCommand` validates the displayed index and enrolment, preserves the active course-class filter,
logs the scope and status transition without logging student names or telehandles, and returns a success message.
`LogicManager` then stores an undo snapshot and saves the updated course-class book together with the undo history

### Removing a student from a class group: `dstudent`
The `dstudent` command removes one student's enrolment from one class group. It does not delete the student globally,
and it does not affect the student's enrolments in other class groups. A student's telehandle identifies the student,
while the class group and module identify the specific enrolment.

`DeleteStudentCommandParser` rejects commands with missing or duplicate prefixes, a non-empty preamble, or invalid

The command uses a two-step confirmation flow to prevent accidental removal:
1. `DeleteStudentCommand#execute` locates the `CourseClass` using the class group and module. If the class does not
exist, it returns `Class group not found: CLASS_GROUP in MODULE_NAME`.
2. The command checks whether the class contains the supplied telehandle. If not, it returns
`Student @TELEHANDLE is not enrolled in CLASS_GROUP in MODULE_NAME`.
3. Before confirmation, the command returns a preview message and does not modify the model.
5. A subsequent `yes` creates a confirmed copy of the command. The command removes the student from the target
`CourseClass`, and `LogicManager` persists the updated `CourseClassBook` and undo history through
6. A subsequent `no` clears the pending command and returns a cancellation message without changing or saving data.
7. Any other confirmation input returns an error and leaves the pending deletion unchanged, allowing the user to
The model operation is scoped to the selected class: `CourseClass#removeStudent` delegates to
`UniqueStudentList#remove`, which removes the student by telehandle. Because each `CourseClass` owns its own enrolled
student list, removing an enrolment from one class does not remove the same student from another class.

The `undo` command restores the course-class data to the state before the most recent successful data-changing command. It uses a last-in-first-out stack of complete `CourseClassBook` snapshots. Each snapshot includes course-class metadata, enrolled students, notes, class homework status, and individual homework overrides.

`AddressBookParser` routes `undo` to `UndoCommandParser`, which accepts no arguments. `Command#isMutating()` identifies commands that can change course-class data. Before such a command executes, `LogicManager` copies the current course-class book. The snapshot is added to the undo stack only after the command succeeds and actually changes the stored data.
Commands that create undo snapshots include:
Search, list, help, and exit do not create snapshots. Failed commands and cancelled `dstudent` confirmations do not create snapshots. A preview is not recorded; only a confirmed deletion is.
When `undo` executes, `ModelManager` removes the latest snapshot from its `Deque<CourseClassBook>` and restores it. Repeating `undo` walks backwards through the stack. Redo is not implemented.

Undo uses the existing course-class JSON storage rather than a separate storage system. `JsonCourseClassBookStorage` saves the current book and snapshots together in `data/courseclasses.json`. The existing `courseClasses` data remains, with an `undoHistory` list containing serialized previous books.

`MainApp` loads both the current book and `undoHistory` into `ModelManager`. After successful commands, `LogicManager` saves both; undo saves the restored current state and the remaining history. Older JSON files without `undoHistory` remain compatible and start with an empty undo stack.
Course-class saves use a temporary file before moving the completed data into place. An atomic move is used when supported, with a replacement fallback otherwise.
* Snapshot history was chosen to keep related course-class data consistent and avoid requiring every command to implement its own inverse operation.
* Storing complete snapshots uses more memory and storage than storing command-specific inverse data. A history limit could be considered in the future.
* Reusing the existing JSON file keeps current data and undo history together across application restarts.

`UndoCommandTest` covers restoration and an empty undo stack. `UndoLogicIntegrationTest` covers last-in-first-out behaviour, class deletion, student removal, homework status, failed and cancelled commands, and restart persistence. `MainAppTest` verifies startup history loading, while storage tests verify round-trip persistence and compatibility with legacy JSON without `undoHistory`.

1. Aiken Duet should work on any _mainstream OS_ with Java `25` installed.
2. Aiken Duet should respond to add, edit, delete, list, and find commands within 2 seconds when storing up to 100 classes and 1,000 students on a typical laptop.

3. A teaching assistant who is familiar with CLI applications should be able to create a class, add a student, find that student, and record an observation within 15 minutes of first using Aiken Duet with the User Guide available.
4. Aiken Duet should store its data locally and should not transmit student information over a network unless the user explicitly initiates such an operation.
5. Invalid commands should not modify existing class, student, enrolment, or teaching-observation data, and should not cause Aiken Duet to terminate unexpectedly.
6. Aiken Duet should parse and save application data within 2 seconds.
7. Should the local save file be corrupted, the system should not overwrite the corrupted file with a blank slate and should alert the user of the error.
8. The data file must be saved in a standard location such as a data folder at the root directory.
9. The teaching assistant should only need the JAR file to run the application and should not need to install any
10. Saved data should be in an easy to edit format for ease of changing in case of save data corruption.
* **Class**: A course offering managed in Aiken Duet and identified by a course code.
* **Class group**: A tutorial, laboratory, or recitation group belonging to a class.
* **Class tag**: A user-defined label used to categorize a class.
* **Consultation**: A scheduled meeting between a teaching assistant and a student, together with any recorded date and topic.
* **Enrolment**: The association between a student and a class group.
* **Follow-up task**: An action that a teaching assistant needs to complete after a class, consultation, or student interaction.
* **Homework**: Work assigned to an individual student for completion outside class.
* **Mainstream OS**: Windows, Linux, Unix, or macOS.
* **Participation**: A record of a student's engagement during a class.
* **Student**: A learner whose details, class-group enrolments, and teaching observations are managed in Aiken Duet.
* **Task**: A teaching-related duty tracked by a teaching assistant, which may have a status, priority, schedule, tag, or time record.
* **Teaching observation**: A timestamped note about a student in the context of a specific class group.
* **Telehandle**: A student's username on a messaging platform used for communication.
* **Typical laptop**: A computer with at least a 2 GHz dual-core processor and 8 GB of RAM.

Aiken Duet is a **desktop application for Teaching Assistants (TA) to manage students in their classes, optimized for use through a Command Line Interface (CLI)** while retaining the benefits of a Graphical User Interface (GUI).

1. Copy the file to an empty, writable folder that you want to use as the _home folder_ for Aiken Duet.
1. Open a terminal, `cd` to the folder containing the JAR file, and run `java -jar addressbook.jar`.
A GUI similar to the one below should appear in a few seconds. Note how the app contains some sample data.

1. Refer to the [Features](#features) section below for details of each command.
* Words in `UPPER_CASE` are the parameters to be supplied by the user.
For example, in `add n/NAME`, replace `NAME` with a value such as `John Doe`.
* Items in square brackets are optional.
For example, `n/NAME [t/TAG]` can be used as `n/John Doe t/friend` or as `n/John Doe`.
* Items followed by `…`​ can appear zero or more times.
For example, `[t/TAG]…​` may be omitted, or written as `t/friend` or `t/friend t/family`.
* Parameters can be in any order unless a command states otherwise.
For example, if the command specifies `n/NAME p/PHONE_NUMBER`, `p/PHONE_NUMBER n/NAME` is also acceptable.
* Extraneous parameters for commands that take no parameters, such as `help`, `lclass`, `exit`, and `cclass`, are ignored.

* If you are using a PDF version of this document, be careful when copying and pasting commands that span multiple lines as space characters surrounding line-breaks may be omitted when copied over to the application.

### Adding a student to a class group: `add`
Adds a student to an existing class group in a specified module. The module name is required so that class groups with
the same name in different modules are distinguished.
* `CLASS_GROUP` identifies the tutorial, laboratory, or recitation group.
* `MODULE_NAME` identifies the module containing the class group.
* All four prefixes are required. The prefixes can be entered in any order, but each prefix can only be used once.
* The class group must already exist.
* A student cannot be enrolled in the same class group more than once, but may be enrolled in different class groups.
* If the class group does not exist or the student is already enrolled, an error is shown and no data is changed.
* `add n/John Doe t/birdman c/T05 m/CS2103T` adds `John Doe` (@birdman) to `T05` in `CS2103T`.
The application displays `John Doe has been successfully added to T05 in CS2103T`.
Edits an existing course class identified by its index in the displayed course-class list. Existing values are
overwritten by the supplied values. Enrolled students and their notes are preserved.
* `INDEX` identifies the course class in the displayed list and must be a positive integer.
* At least one field must be supplied. The `n/` and `c/` prefixes can each be used at most once.
* `t/TAG` replaces the complete set of tags. To remove all tags, use `t/` with no value.
* The edited class group and module combination must not duplicate another course class.
* `eclass 1 n/L01 t/lab` updates the first displayed course class to `L01` and replaces its tags with `lab`.
Sets the homework status for a displayed course class or for one student enrolled in that class. The class status is
the default inherited by students without an individual override. Statuses are shown on the class and student cards,
* `INDEX` identifies the course class in the displayed list and must be a positive integer.
* The class-wide `STATUS` must be one of `pending`, `completed`, or `not-set`.
* The individual form overrides the class default for the enrolled student identified by `TELEHANDLE`.
* Use `s/inherit` with the individual form to clear that override and return the student to the class default.
* Updating homework status does not change student details or notes.
* If the class list is filtered, the current filter remains active after the status is updated.
* `hwork 1 s/completed` marks the first displayed course class's homework as completed for the whole class.
* `hwork 1 t/alice_tan s/completed` marks only Alice's homework as completed in the first displayed class.
* `hwork 1 t/alice_tan s/inherit` makes Alice inherit the first displayed class's current status again.
Deletes a course class identified by its index in the displayed course-class list. The course class and its enrolled
students and notes are removed from the course-class book without a confirmation prompt.
* `INDEX` identifies the course class in the displayed list and must be a positive integer.
* `dclass 1` deletes the first displayed course class.
If the deletion was accidental, enter `undo` immediately afterwards to restore the deleted course class.
Adds a class group to the system.
* When adding or renaming a class, `NAME` cannot contain `n/`, `t/`, `c/`, `m/`, `i/` or `o/` immediately after a space.
* `COURSE_CODE` identifies the module containing the class group. When adding or changing it, it must not be blank
and is limited to 50 characters, including spaces. It can contain English letters, digits, spaces, `#`, `@` and `$`.
* `t/TAG` is optional and can be provided multiple times.
* The `n/` and `c/` prefixes are required and can be entered in either order. Each can be used only once.
When `n/` comes first, the full text up to `c/` is treated as the class name. Put actual `t/` tags after `c/`.
* A class is considered a duplicate when it has the same name and course code as an existing class, regardless of tags.
* After a class is added, it appears in the class list and is saved automatically.
* `aclass n/F10-2 c/CS2103T` adds a class group without tags.
* `aclass n/F10-2 c/CS2103T t/tutorial t/odd-week` adds a class group with two tags.
If the required prefixes are missing, duplicated, or contain invalid values, the application shows the command format
and does not add the class. Attempting to add an existing class shows `This class already exists in the system.`
Previously saved names and course codes remain loadable, including undo history. If an older class name contains
command prefixes, use `eclass INDEX n/NEW_NAME` to rename it before using student/note commands for that class.
### Removing a student from a class group: `dstudent`
Removes a student's enrolment from one class group without removing the student's enrolments in other classes.
The student is identified by their telehandle, while the class group and module identify the enrolment to remove.
The module name is required so that class groups with the same name in different modules are distinguished.
* `CLASS_GROUP` identifies the tutorial, laboratory, or recitation group.
* `MODULE_NAME` identifies the module containing the class group.
* All three prefixes are required. The prefixes can be entered in any order, but each prefix can only be used once.
* The command first displays the matching student and asks for confirmation before changing any data.
* Type `yes` to remove the enrolment, or `no` to cancel without changing any data.
* If the input is neither `yes` nor `no`, the application asks for a valid confirmation again and keeps the deletion pending.
* If the class group or enrolment cannot be found, an error is shown and no data is changed.
The application displays `Remove John Doe (@birdman) from T05 in CS2103T? Type yes to confirm or no to cancel.`
The application displays `Student @birdman has been removed from T05 in CS2103T`.
If the removal was accidental, enter `undo` immediately afterwards to restore the student to the class.
To cancel the operation, enter `no` after the confirmation prompt. The application displays
`Student deletion cancelled. No records were changed.`

Displays all course classes in the course-class book.
Removes all course classes from the course-class book, including their enrolled students and notes.
If the clearing was accidental, enter `undo` immediately afterwards to restore the course classes.
Restores the course-class data to the state before the most recent successful data-changing command.
Undo supports changes to course classes, student enrolments, notes, homework statuses, and clearing the course-class
book. For example, enter `undo` after `dclass 1` to restore the deleted class, or after confirming a `dstudent`
command to restore the removed student.
* Undo changes are applied one at a time, starting with the most recent change.
* You can enter `undo` repeatedly to reverse earlier successful changes.
* Failed commands and cancelled student-deletion confirmations do not create undo entries.
* Search, list, help, and exit commands do not create undo entries.
* Undo history is saved in `data/courseclasses.json` and remains available after restarting the application.
* The application does not currently provide a `redo` command.
If there is no saved change to undo, the application displays `There is no change to undo.`
The application automatically saves the course-class data and undo history after every command that completes
successfully. You do not need to save manually.
Course-class data and undo history are saved automatically as a JSON file
`[JAR file location]/data/courseclasses.json`. Advanced users are welcome to update data directly by editing that data
If your changes make the data file invalid, the application starts with an empty course-class book at the next run. The
invalid file remains on disk until you run a command (the application saves after every successful command). Still, we
recommend backing up the file before editing it.
Furthermore, certain edits can cause the application to behave in unexpected ways (e.g., if a value entered is outside
of the acceptable range). Therefore, edit the data file only if you are confident that you can update it correctly.
**Q**: How do I transfer my data to another computer?
**A**: Install the app on the other computer and overwrite the `data/courseclasses.json` file it creates with the file
from your previous Aiken Duet home folder.
